prediction: #433 lane.bf2stall433, after the vertex-RAM mirror arm refuted V (pilot pair: heavy-view GPU ms B/A = 36.0/35.9 with the IO-coherent premise confirmed). TU_DEBUG=syncdraw makes Turnip wait for idle (WAIT_FOR_IDLE + WAIT_FOR_ME + WAIT_MEM_WRITES) before EVERY draw (tu6_emit_flushes via tu_emit_cache_flush_renderpass; sysmem so it is once per draw, not once per bin). That separates the two shapes the 12-14 us per draw can have. S: the draws are ALREADY serialized by something in the command stream (each draw waits on the one before, e.g. the per-draw descriptor rebind with bindless invalidation and constant reload). Then forcing a drain per draw adds little. T: the draws normally overlap and the per-draw cost is throughput (shader and constant work). Then a drain per draw adds the whole pipeline depth to every draw, ~5-20 us each at ~2,000 draws.

what_follows: S: the fix is to stop serializing draws. The candidate is the per-draw UBO rebind (a new dynamic offset every draw, hence a new descriptor set, bindless invalidation and a constant reload): bind the uniform data once per pass and index it per draw. That is vk/shaders.c and the GLSL generators, outside this lane's territory. T: the cost is work, not waiting, and the lever is the per-draw shader/constant cost (the size of the uniform block reloaded per draw, the ubershader's per-draw cost), measured with Adreno counters (TU_DEBUG=perfc exposes VK_KHR_performance_query).
